selection_warning: The legacy pilot pair below was selected after a targeted search for a later controlled study and remains outside Paper 3 scoring. The new bounded adjudication in this artifact is separately identified by artifact_id and preserves the frozen 13-question labels.

source.source_question: Whether natural-language code generation/retrieval in an IDE improves developer productivity or accuracy in realistic developer tasks.
source.source_observation: The authors' multi-task plugin study reports positive qualitative experience but inconclusive quantitative productivity, quality, and correctness effects.
source.locator: PDF page 1, abstract; treatment is a hybrid code generation/retrieval PyCharm plugin across 14 Python tasks.

later_primary_evidence.design: 95 recruited professional programmers randomly assigned to Copilot access (45) or control (50), tasked with building a JavaScript HTTP server; reported main time comparison conditions on the 70 participants who completed task and survey.
later_primary_evidence.reported_time_difference: Mean 71.17 versus 160.89 minutes among completers, a 55.8% shorter completion time for the treatment; reported 95% CI for reduction 21%-89%, t-test p=0.0017.
later_primary_evidence.reported_success_rate: Treatment success-rate difference of 7 percentage points was not statistically significant (reported 95% CI -11 to +25 percentage points).
later_primary_evidence.locator: PDF pages 2-7, Study Design, Results, Discussion

adjudication.reason: Different assistant (hybrid PyCharm retrieval/generation versus Copilot), different language/tasks and participant pools; the 2023 time result is conditional on completion, with an imprecise success-rate effect. The study itself does not assess code quality or general professional-project productivity.

next_required_step: Freeze a larger question cohort and label rubric before searching for follow-ups; keep this hand-selected pilot out of Paper 3 benchmark scoring.

frozen_rubric.outcome_window: strictly after each source as_of timestamp through frozen three_year_followup_end inclusive
frozen_rubric.direct_supported: An independently dated in-window primary source directly tests the same question, object and metric or proves the same formal claim with explicit assumptions and enough evidence for the prespecified success criterion.
frozen_rubric.direct_refuted_or_premise_revised: An independently dated in-window primary source directly falsifies the specified claim or shows that a central premise fails under the stated conditions.
frozen_rubric.explicitly_unresolved: An in-window primary source explicitly states that the same question remains open or reports a direct inconclusive/negative test under relevant conditions.
frozen_rubric.unadjudicated: No directly matching, date-verified evidence is authenticated, or the match/conditions are ambiguous; search non-detection is not a negative outcome.

source_and_question.source_title: Towards Characterizing Adversarial Defects of Deep Learning Software from the Lens of Uncertainty

source_text_verification.locator: PDF p. 11, §8 Conclusion and Future Work; source-screen record reports the same version and hash
source_text_verification.observed_claim: The source characterizes and generates uncommon-uncertainty adversarial examples, and leaves using those examples to enhance robustness as future work; evasion-generation results are not training evidence.

source_and_question.frozen_question: At equal training-example count and compute, does training on uncommon-uncertainty adversarial examples improve held-out robust accuracy over conventional adversarial training without materially degrading clean accuracy?
source_and_question.frozen_falsification_gate: No held-out robustness advantage, or prespecified clean-accuracy degradation, fails the proposed benefit.

follow_up_source.title: Guiding the retraining of convolutional neural networks against adversarial inputs
follow_up_source.date_verification: PeerJ/PMC article header records 2023 Aug 8; received 2023-03-20 and accepted 2023-06-06.
full_text_sections_inspected: Empirical study: Research questions and Variables
verified_follow_up_claims: The study evaluates five image-classification datasets and CNN models.
Adversarial training and test inputs are generated with FGSM, BIM, and CW; the training set combines original and adversarial inputs.
Guidance metrics are NC, DSA, LSA, Random, DeepGini, and softmax entropy; the study compares OAR, AR, and AF retraining configurations.

The accuracy endpoint uses an augmented held-out test set containing original and adversarial test inputs; the paper reports uncertainty metrics as often selecting inputs with the best observed accuracy and AR as favorable under its design.
evidence_locators: HTML §§ Empirical study, Variables, and Study design
HTML § Model training: adversarial inputs and FGSM/BIM/CW construction; OAR/AR/AF definitions
HTML §§ Threats to validity and Conclusions/future work

match_audit.reason: The follow-up studies uncertainty-guided ordering of adversarial inputs generated by standard attacks. It does not use the source paper's uncommon-uncertainty adversarial-example generator, does not compare that intervention with conventional adversarial training at equal example count and compute, and does not report a prespecified clean-accuracy trade-off for that comparison. Its augmented adversarial accuracy endpoint is related but not sufficient.

observed_result_or_blocker.result: Near-match only: independent dated follow-up evidence strengthens the broader premise that uncertainty-guided adversarial retraining can improve the study's augmented-test accuracy/resource trade-off within its CNN, dataset, attack, and configuration choices.
observed_result_or_blocker.label: unadjudicated
observed_result_or_blocker.negative_result_preserved: No direct positive, negative, or explicit-unresolved outcome for the frozen uncommon-uncertainty intervention was authenticated.

uncertainty: This is one near-match and cannot distinguish uncertainty-based selection from ordinary adversarial retraining, attack choice, or configuration effects.
The follow-up reports best observed values across retraining data points; it is not the frozen equal-count/equal-compute comparison.
The source/follow-up pair is suitable for evidence-gap refinement, not Paper 3 outcome scoring.
adjudications.next_falsifiable_action: Locate or execute, under a newly preregistered protocol that preserves this frozen question, a dated primary comparison using the 2004.11573 uncommon-uncertainty generator versus conventional adversarial training, equalized training-example count and compute, held-out attack families, clean accuracy, robust accuracy, independent seeds, and a prespecified material-degradation threshold.
